Nivel de vechime: Nivel mediu de experiență
Tip de angajare: Full-time
Sectoare de activitate: Servicii IT și consultanță IT
Understand the signal. Find the cause. Make the instrument work reliably. 
 An unexpected measurement can come from the sensor, the electronics, the timing or the firmware. If you enjoy following that trail from code to hardware, this role could suit you.
 At ERNI, you will work with a customer developing instruments for vacuum measurement, leak detection and process control. Your firmware will connect the physical measurement to the behaviour of the instrument.
 The work 
 You will develop and improve embedded firmware in C and C++, working mainly on bare-metal ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers.
 Together with electronics and other engineering colleagues, you will turn product requirements into working functionality, investigate issues on real hardware and verify that your changes behave as intended.
 Your work will include:
Developing firmware for sensor interfaces, instrument functions and communication with connected systems
Bringing up and debugging hardware with electronics engineers, using schematics, datasheets and lab measurements
Extending existing firmware as well as implementing new functionality
Building tests that make changes easier to verify and faults easier to reproduce
Investigating issues found during development, production or use in the field
 The technical environment includes STM32-class microcontrollers, peripheral interfaces such as SPI, I²C and UART, and communication protocols such as CAN and Modbus. The interfaces you work with will depend on the instrument.
 What you should already bring 
Professional experience developing embedded firmware, with strong C skills and practical experience using C++
Experience working directly with microcontrollers and bare-metal firmware, including peripherals, interrupts and timing constraints
The ability to investigate hardware-software issues using a debugger, schematics and measurement equipment
A disciplined approach to testing, code review and version control
German & English skills that allow you to discuss technical problems and collaborate with international colleagues
Experience with ARM Cortex-M is particularly relevant. If you have worked with another microcontroller family, explain what you developed and how closely you worked with the hardware.
 What you can build on 
 You do not need previous experience in vacuum technology or every protocol in the product portfolio.
 Experience with STM32, automated embedded testing, industrial communication, bootloaders or signal processing would give you useful starting points. The core requirement is the ability to understand an embedded system, make sound changes and demonstrate that they work.
 Why this work may interest you 
 This role offers a direct connection between software and physical behaviour. You can trace a problem from an instrument’s response to the firmware and electronics behind it, then verify the effect of your solution on real hardware.
 It suits someone who enjoys both developing functionality and understanding why an existing system behaves unexpectedly.
 What We Offer 
Medical services subscription
22 days of holiday per year + 1 additional day per year of service (up to 27)
Company loyalty bonus after 3, 5, and 10 years
Meal tickets
Monthly budget for sport subscriptions
Access to e-learning platforms (Pluralsight)
Fruits, coffee, and tea in the office
Regular company events
